query: How can ERP/GL ledger codes be mapped to module assemblies in practice—show a worked example for pooled overhead allocations and synthetic ledger snapshot?

response.query: How can ERP/GL ledger codes be mapped to module assemblies in practice—show a worked example for pooled overhead allocations and synthetic ledger snapshot?
response.answer: ERP/GL ledger codes map to module assemblies by configuring project account groups and linking expense accounts to these groups for pooled overhead allocations. This setup allows for automatic posting of timecard data to both the general ledger and project modules.

ERP – General Ledger and Accounting Management ERP – General Ledger and Accounting Management Financial accounting module of an ERP package provides company wide control and integration of financial information. This module provides the ability to centrally track financial accounting data within a framework of multiple companies, languages and currencies. Through integration with logistics, business processes as well as with accounting sub ledgers of other finance modules such as accounts payable, accounts receivable, cash management, GL provides a central pool of accounting data required for finance reporting (including statutory reports) and other purpose. **GL master data set up:** One of the important processes of GL is setting up chart of Accounts, which is a complete structure of ledger accounts used by the organization. Other important parameters of GL are i) parent company and company parameters (this will contain accounts for profit and loss, currency fluctuations etc. ii) Periods (Fiscal and Tax), iii) Tax code by countries **GL integration set up with logistics modules:** Integration mapping scheme needs to be defined for posting of logistics transactions into finance. results.title: Timecard Accounting for Projects in Acumatica Cloud ERP
results.content:
Title: Timecard Accounting for Projects in Acumatica Cloud ERP
# Technical Tuesday: Timecard Accounting for Projects in Acumatica Cloud ERP. *Acumatica cloud ERP users have options for managing their timecard accounting for projects. Today’s Technical Tuesday post will discuss the advantages of different methods, each one dependent on how payroll is implemented and on reporting requirements.*. Acumatica cloud ERP provides different timecard posting options. This allows customers to pass expenses to projects and properly account for activities which are entered onto timecards. Customers using timecards have different payroll implementations and reporting requirements which influence which implementation option is best for a specific business. Timecard data can be used for payroll, project billing, budget tracking, and reporting. Depending on your needs, you can configure Acumatica’s cloud ERP software to post transactions to the general ledger and the project modules. This requires that timecard information is posted to the general ledger. This requires that timecard information is passed to the project. This can be accomplished by posting to the general ledger or the project module. **Situation 4**: Your business requires employees to log hours on projects and overhead hours in order to produce detailed reports which describe the ratio of time worked on projects versus overhead time. ## Implementation and Benefits of Posting to the General Ledger and Project. Post transactions to the general ledger when you need to send timecard data to payroll or when you need financial reports that split project hours from non-project hours. This scenario is implemented in the SalesDemo data that you can download as a snapshot on the Acumatica portal. This option causes the system to create general ledger transactions when a project is specified on a time activity. A project transaction will also be created if the general ledger code is mapped to a project account group. Within project preferences, you can set the account source for the debit (expense account) and credit (accrual account) transactions for the project transactions. When entering a labor item, the ***expense account*** must be set to an expense account that is linked to a project account group. If the expense accrual account is not linked to a project account group, then the credit account will be created for the GL entry, but not on the project.

results.title: General Ledger Module Overview
results.content: The module consists of a complete integration of accounts receivable, accounts payable, and inventory with the General Ledger (GL) Module. The General Ledger Module is used to establish a chart of accounts and to keep track of transactions that flow through the accounts. These transactions are generated from direct manual entries, as well as from "automatic" entries from other sub-ledgers (such as Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Sales Order Processing) if these modules are interfaced to the General Ledger Module. In the standard system, Accounts Payable is already interfaced with the General Ledger. Sales Order Processing is interfaced with Accounts Receivable, and these modules can be interfaced to the General Ledger with program GPTM, Posting Template Maintenance, and setting the Interface AR to GL flag to on. The several query programs in the General Ledger (GL) Module give users the opportunity to trace the status of transactions from the time they are first journalized to the time they are posted into the general ledger. The module also contains general ledger posting and account balance inquiry programs. Periodic reports generated by the General Ledger (GL) Module include the Detail and Summary Trial Balance. Distributions, allocation journals, and manual journal entries can contain account numbers for more than one enterprise. * All account numbers must conform to their enterprise's rules of validity before the entry will be posted anywhere. There is only one general-purpose account assignment and journal move/post interface. Account distribution codes can be used anywhere that a general ledger account number may be entered. Instead of closing each period, NDS Applications requires that summary accounts exists for income and expense accounts, and in comparing these accounts at any time, the current earnings (profit/loss) can be seen. In the general ledger balance sheet, be sure to include the income and expense accounts as hidden accounts, or if you have a summary account set up to summarize the income and expense, include it in the balance sheet. * GLPC (Final) GL Period Close Processing - Year end closure nets out income and expense accounts to retained earnings and zeros out beginning balances for the next fiscal year.
